sents.en: A few years ago I found myself teaching a university class on evil.
sents.cn: 几年前，我在大学里讲授一门关于"恶"的课程。

sents.en: It was for third-year criminology students to help them contextualize theory and research within controversial current topics.
sents.cn: 它面向犯罪学三年级学生，旨在帮助他们在有争议的时事话题中理解理论与研究。

sents.en: It was a huge success. The debates were heated and interesting. I could see people's views change within the course of a single lecture.
sents.cn: 这门课大获成功，辩论热烈而精彩，我能看到人们的观点在一场讲座之内就发生改变。

sents.en: Over the past 13 years, as a student, lecturer and researcher, I've enjoyed discussing the science of evil with anyone willing to listen.
sents.cn: 在过去的13年里，作为学生、讲师和研究者，我一直乐于与任何愿意倾听的人讨论"恶"的科学。

sents.en: What I like most is destroying the cliché (陈词滥调) of good and evil, and replacing them with scientific insight.
sents.cn: 我最喜欢的，就是打破关于善与恶的陈词滥调，用科学的洞见取而代之。

sents.en: We need a more informed way of discussing behavior that at first we cannot, or should not, begin to understand.
sents.cn: 对于那些我们起初无法、也不该贸然去理解的行为，我们需要一种更有依据的讨论方式。

sents.en: Without understanding, we risk dehumanizing others, writing off human beings simply because we don't comprehend them.
sents.cn: 如果不加理解，我们就可能把他人"非人化"，仅仅因为无法理解就把他们一笔勾销。

sents.en: We must try to understand what we have labeled evil.
sents.cn: 我们必须努力去理解那些被我们贴上"恶"的标签的事物。

sents.en: We tend to think evil is something that other people are.
sents.cn: 我们往往认为恶是别人的属性。

sents.en: We think of ourselves as "good people", and even when we do morally wrong things, we understand the context of our decisions.
sents.cn: 我们把自己当作"好人"，即便做了道德上错误的事，也明白自己决定的前因后果。

sents.en: With others, however, it is far easier to write them off.
sents.cn: 然而对别人，要把他们一笔勾销就容易得多。

sents.en: If their actions deviate (偏离) substantially from what we consider acceptable, we may label them evil.
sents.cn: 如果他们的行为严重偏离我们认为可以接受的范围，我们可能会给他们贴上"恶"的标签。

sents.en: We need to be careful with this.
sents.cn: 对此我们必须谨慎。

sents.en: Calling someone evil is often similar to saying they cannot change, and perhaps aren't even a human at all.
sents.cn: 称某人为恶人，往往等于断言他无可救药，甚至根本不配为人。

sents.en: However, when you actually go monster-hunting, and you look deeply at the people behind shocking behavior, you may be surprised.
sents.cn: 然而，当你真的去"猎怪"，深入审视那些骇人行为背后的普通人时，你也许会大吃一惊。

sents.en: As a child I used to love the Scooby-Doo cartoons.
sents.cn: 小时候我很爱看《史酷比》动画片。

sents.en: Arriving in their "Mystery Machine", the gang would have to find a monster who was terrorizing a neighborhood.
sents.cn: 主角们开着"神秘机器"赶到某处，去揪出恐吓街坊的怪物。

sents.en: They would run around looking for clues and at the end unmask the bad guy. It was always a normal person in a costume. There were no monsters.
sents.cn: 他们四处寻找线索，最后揭穿坏人的真面目——那总是一个穿着怪物道具服的普通人，世上本没有怪物。

sents.en: Like the Scooby crew, we may find ourselves hunting for an easy fix, one word for people who do bad things.
sents.cn: 和史酷比一行人一样，我们也常常想找一个简单的答案，用一个词来概括做坏事的人。

sents.en: But if we take a good look, the word "evil" is insufficient·there are no simple explanations for why humans do bad things; instead there are many, and they are all marvelously different.
sents.cn: 但只要仔细看就会发现，"恶"这个词并不够用——人类做坏事的原因没有简单的解释，相反，原因有很多，而且都千差万别、令人惊叹。

sents.en: Evil is typically referred to when there is deviance from social norms; formal deviance is the violation of laws, like theft, murder, and attacks, while informal deviance involves violations of social norms, like lying.
sents.cn: 通常，当行为偏离社会规范时，人们就会谈到"恶"。正式越轨指违反法律，如盗窃、谋杀和袭击；非正式越轨则指违反社会规范，如撒谎。

sents.en: Evil behavior is typically thought to embrace one or both forms.
sents.cn: 恶行通常被认为涵盖其中一种或两种形式。

sents.en: However, deviance can also describe a behavior that simply differs from the norm.
sents.cn: 然而，越轨也可以描述一种仅仅不同于常规的行为。

sents.en: Perhaps this is where we can find the good side of our bad side.
sents.cn: 也许正是在这里，我们能发现自己人性中坏的一面所带来的好的一面。

sents.en: Deviating from the norm can make us villains (恶棍), but it can also make us heroes.
sents.cn: 偏离常规可以让我们沦为恶棍，也可以让我们成为英雄。

sents.en: A child deviates from social pressures when they stand up for another child being bullied in school.
sents.cn: 当一个孩子顶住同伴压力、挺身保护在学校被霸凌的另一个孩子时，他是在越轨；

sents.en: A soldier deviates when they choose not to follow orders to kill an innocent civilian.
sents.cn: 当一名士兵拒绝执行杀害无辜平民的命令时，他是在越轨；

sents.en: An employee in a big tech company deviates when they expose its wrongdoings.
sents.cn: 当一家大科技公司的员工揭露公司的恶行时，他也是在越轨。

sents.en: Creativity is also a deviation.
sents.cn: 创造力同样是一种越轨。

sents.en: Here, too, things are complex.
sents.cn: 在这件事上，情况同样复杂。

sents.en: Thinking creatively has given us modern medicine, technology and modern political structures, but it has also given us poison and nuclear weapons.
sents.cn: 创造性思维带给我们现代医学、技术和现代政治制度，但也带给我们毒药和核武器。

sents.en: Great benefit and great harm can come from the same human tendency.
sents.cn: 巨大的益处与巨大的危害，可能出自同一种人类倾向。

sents.en: In a research paper, Evil Genius, published in 2014, the behavioral scientists Francesca Gino and Scott Wiltermuth wanted to examine whether people who behave unethically in one task are more creative than others on a subsequent task, even after controlling for differences in baseline creative skills.
sents.cn: 在2014年发表的研究论文《邪恶天才》中，行为科学家弗朗西斯卡∙吉诺和斯科特∙维尔特穆斯想要探究：那些在第一项任务中行为不道德的人，在随后的任务中是否比别人更有创造力——即便控制了基线创造力水平的差异之后依然如此。

sents.en: The unethical behavior they chose was dishonesty.
sents.cn: 他们选择的不道德行为是不诚实。

sents.en: Over five experiments researchers gave participants tasks in which they could cheat.
sents.cn: 在共计五项实验中，研究者给参与者布置了可以作弊的任务。

sents.en: In one study, they were given matrices (矩阵) and had to find two numbers that added up to 10.
sents.cn: 在其中一项研究里，参与者拿到一组矩阵，必须找出两个加起来等于10的数字。

sents.en: Participants were asked to self-report how well they did at the end of the study; 59% cheated by saying that they solved more matrices than they actually had.
sents.cn: 研究结束时，参与者被要求自我报告成绩；59%的人撒了谎，声称自己解出的矩阵比实际的多。

sents.en: After each task, the researchers measured participants' performance on the Remote Associates Test.
sents.cn: 每项任务结束后，研究者都会测量参与者在"远程联想测验"中的表现。

sents.en: This shows participants three words at a time that appear to be unrelated, and the person has to think of a fourth word that is associated with all of them.
sents.cn: 该测验每次向参与者呈现三个看似互不相关的词，受试者必须想出与这三个词都有关联的第四个词。

sents.en: For example, you might get "Fox, Man, Peep", or "Dust, Cereal, Fish".
sents.cn: 例如，你可能得到"狐狸、男人、偷看"，或"灰尘、麦片、鱼"。

sents.en: In order to find the linking words ("Hole" for the first, "Bowl" for the second) you need to be creative.
sents.cn: 要找出那个联系词（前者的答案是"洞"，后者是"碗"），你需要发挥创造力。

sents.en: The more you get right, the more creative you are thought to be because you have come up with uncommon associations.
sents.cn: 答对的越多，就说明你越有创造力，因为你想到了不寻常的联想。

sents.en: For every one of the five studies, they found the same thing·participants who cheated in the first task did better on the creativity task.
sents.cn: 在全部五项研究中，他们都发现了同样的结果——第一项任务中作弊的参与者在创造力任务上表现得更好。为什么？

sents.en: Why? Like other forms of unethical behavior, lying means breaking rules. It involves being deviant, going against the social principle that people should tell the truth.
sents.cn: 与其他形式的不道德行为一样，撒谎意味着打破规则，它包含越轨，违背"人应当诚实"的社会准则。

sents.en: Similarly, being creative involves "thinking outside the box", deviating from expectations.
sents.cn: 同样，有创造力也需要"跳出框框思考"，偏离预期。

sents.en: They involve similar thought patterns, so stimulating one stimulates the other.
sents.cn: 两者涉及相似的思维模式，因此刺激其一便会带动其二。

sents.en: Can we learn from this?
sents.cn: 我们能从中学习吗？

sents.en: Perhaps.
sents.cn: 也许可以。

sents.en: To be more creative, we could try lying in a controlled environment. Find online logic games and cheat at them, play Scrabble (拼字游戏) with a dictionary, or write a story about something that is untrue?
sents.cn: 为了更有创造力，我们可以在可控的环境中尝试撒谎：找一些在线逻辑游戏并作弊，借助词典玩拼字游戏，或者写一个虚构的故事。

sents.en: Such tasks can get our brains thinking flexibly, beyond our normal comfort zone.
sents.cn: 这类任务能让大脑灵活思考，走出我们惯常的舒适区。

sents.en: This is not a call to become a compulsive (强迫性的) liar, but a controlled liar.
sents.cn: 这不是号召大家变成病态说谎者，而是做一名"受控的"说谎者。

sents.en: In addition to benefits for creativity, deviance can be a good thing in other ways.
sents.cn: 除了对创造力有益之外，越轨在其他方面也可以是好事。

sents.en: Even Philip Zimbardo, the author of the Stanford prison experiment, who showed how easily we can be led to behave badly, believes that the future of deviance research may lie more in understanding extreme prosocial behavior, such as heroism.
sents.cn: 就连斯坦福监狱实验的设计者菲利普∙津巴多——他曾展示我们是多么容易被引向恶行——也相信，越轨研究的未来或许更多在于理解极端的亲社会行为，例如英雄主义。

sents.en: Like evil, we often view heroism as only a possibility for outliers·for people who are abnormal.
sents.cn: 与"恶"一样，我们常把英雄主义视为只有异类——那些不正常的人——才可能拥有的东西。

sents.en: But Zimbardo asks: "What if the capability to act heroically is also fundamentally ordinary and available to all of us?" Some say we should never meet our heroes, lest they disappoint us when we find out how normal they are.
sents.cn: 但津巴多问道："如果挺身而出的英雄气概从根本上说也是一种寻常品质，我们人人都具备呢？"有人说永远不要去见自己心中的英雄，免得发现他们其实平凡如你我而感到失望。

sents.en: But this should be liberating, not disappointing.
sents.cn: 但这应当是令人解脱的，而非令人失望的。

sents.en: We are all capable of behaving like outliers.
sents.cn: 我们所有人都有做出非凡之举的潜能。

sents.en: It's time for us to understand deviance, and realize its potential for good as well as for harm.
sents.cn: 现在是时候去理解越轨，并认识到它既可为害、亦可为善的潜力了。
